about.title: Westlake Village Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Westlake Village draws steady foot traffic to its shopping centers along Agoura Road and Thousand Oaks Boulevard, along with office parks, restaurants, and community spaces near Lindero Canyon Road. Falls happen for plenty of reasons: a wet floor left unmarked, a cracked walkway, poor lighting in a parking structure, or a spill that sat too long before anyone cleaned it up. Under California law, proving a premises liability claim usually means showing the property owner or manager knew, or reasonably should have known, about the hazard and didn't fix it or warn you in time. That's why documentation matters so much right after a fall — photos of the exact spot, witness names, and a request to preserve any surveillance footage before it's deleted. If you were hurt on someone else's property in Westlake Village, LawProactive can connect you with an independent attorney who can evaluate what happened, free of charge and with no obligation.

whyChoose.title: What Matters in a Westlake Village Premises Case

items.title: Notice Is Everything
items.desc: California requires showing the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard and failed to address it. An attorney can help identify maintenance records, prior complaints, or inspection logs that speak to that notice.

items.title: Video Disappears Fast
items.desc: Many stores and offices overwrite surveillance footage within days or weeks. Getting a formal preservation request out quickly can be the difference between having evidence and having none.

items.title: Comparative Fault Doesn't End Your Claim
items.desc: Even if you're partly at fault for not seeing a hazard, California's pure comparative fault rule still allows recovery reduced by your share of responsibility, so a partial-fault scenario isn't automatically a dead end.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Westlake Village?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit against a private property owner. If a government entity owns or maintains the property, such as a public sidewalk or municipal building, the deadline is much shorter and involves an earlier claim filing requirement. It's worth having an attorney check this early since missing a deadline can end a claim entirely.

items.question: What should I do right after falling at a Westlake Village business?
items.answer: Take photos of the hazard, the surrounding area, and your injuries before anything changes. Ask an employee or manager to file an incident report and get their name, and if there were witnesses nearby, get their contact information too. Seeking medical care promptly also creates a record connecting your injuries to the fall.

items.question: Does it matter which road or shopping area the fall happened near?
items.answer: Not directly for liability, though busier corridors like Agoura Road or Thousand Oaks Boulevard host more retail and commercial properties where falls tend to get reported. What matters legally is whether the specific property owner had notice of the hazard, regardless of which corridor the business sits on.
